creator: Jesse Armstrong
address_as_given: a townhouse on Fifth Avenue, Upper East Side
notes: Press accounts place the townhouse on Fifth Avenue on the Upper East Side; I found no cross street or number given on screen. Graded as neighborhood because Fifth Avenue on the Upper East Side runs some 35 blocks.
source_quote: close to where Logan’s Fifth Avenue townhouse is supposed to be on Manhattan’s Upper East Side.
source2_quote: Patriarch Logan Roy and his wife Marcia live in a townhouse on Fifth Avenue

creator: Jesse Armstrong
address_as_given: American Irish Historical Society, 991 Fifth Avenue
notes: 991 Fifth Avenue plays the townhouse lobby; Untapped says the upper floors are a Silvercup Studios set. Bustle, citing Architectural Digest, says an establishing exterior is a Billionaires’ Row tower, so the outside shot may differ from this building.
source_quote: Key locations included the American Irish Historical Society on Fifth Avenue as the location for Logan's apartment
source2_quote: The lobby of the townhouse is filmed in the American Irish Historical Society at 991 Fifth Avenue located across from the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

creator: Jesse Armstrong
address_as_given: penthouse, 180 East 88th Street
notes: Season 4 (episode 4 onward). The building was used for interior scenes of the penthouse; I found no address for Kendall’s home stated in the show itself.
source_quote: This unit at 180 East 88th Street was used as the home of Kendall Roy on Succession, played by Jeremy Strong, in the latest episode of the series.

household: in the apartment of his ex-wife Rava and their children
creator: Jesse Armstrong
address_as_given: the Pinnacle apartment, Woolworth Tower Residences (entrance 2 Park Place)
notes: Season 3 opening episodes. The apartment is Rava’s; Kendall uses it as his base. Untapped says scenes were shot inside the apartment and at the 2 Park Place entrance.
source_quote: The Pinnacle Apartment within the Woolworth Tower Residences is where Kendall Roy is holing up. His wife and children live there
source2_quote: In previous episodes, Kendall has lived in a penthouse at the Woolworth Building and on the 90th floor of 35 Hudson Yards.

creator: Jesse Armstrong
address_as_given: 90th floor, 35 Hudson Yards
notes: Filming location for one of Kendall’s apartments. I did not confirm which season used it; the years are a best estimate.
source_quote: In previous episodes, Kendall has lived in a penthouse at the Woolworth Building and on the 90th floor of 35 Hudson Yards.

creator: Jesse Armstrong
address_as_given: 714 Broadway
notes: Season 1 filming location for Shiv’s apartment. Whether Tom lives there too in season 1 is not stated in the source.
source_quote: 714 Broadway as the location of Shiv's season 1 apartment

creator: Julian Fellowes
address_as_given: East 61st Street, across from the Russells, at Fifth Avenue
notes: The show puts the van Rhijn house across 61st Street from the Russell mansion at Fifth Avenue; no house number is given. The house is fictional; the corner today has the Pierre and other later buildings.
source_quote: comes to live with her estranged aunts at East 61st Street following the death of her father.
source2_quote: two surprising cameos bring us to the corner of 61st Street and Fifth Avenue.

household: with her sister Ada Brook and niece Marian Brook
creator: Julian Fellowes
address_as_given: backlot set, Old Bethpage, Long Island
notes: Exterior is a backlot set in Nassau County, outside New York City, extended with digital effects. The source spells the street "6lst".
source_quote: Two of the most prominent sets were the Russell and van Rhijn mansions on East 6lst Street, shot on a backlot in Old Bethpage, Long Island.

household: with their children Larry and Gladys
creator: Julian Fellowes
address_as_given: the corner of 61st Street and Fifth Avenue, just off Central Park
notes: Press accounts of the show put the Russell mansion on the corner of East 61st Street and Fifth Avenue, across from the van Rhijn house; I did not confirm the corner is named on screen, so it is graded as inferred. The house is fictional; its design borrows from the Cooper Hewitt and the Lotos Club.
source_quote: two surprising cameos bring us to the corner of 61st Street and Fifth Avenue.
source2_quote: moves into an elaborate Stanford White-designed mansion with wife, Bertha, and their young-adult children, Larry and Gladys.

household: with their children Larry and Gladys

address_as_given: backlot set, Old Bethpage, Long Island
notes: Exterior is a backlot set in Nassau County, outside New York City, extended with digital effects.

source2_quote: This establishing exterior shot was filmed on the show's backlot in Bethpage, Long Island where a strip of building facades were constructed.

creator: Ralph Ellison
address_as_given: a hole in the basement of a building rented strictly to whites, in a border area of Harlem
notes: Quoted from the prologue as first printed in Partisan Review, January 1952. Ellison never says which edge of Harlem; the point is a rough placement on Harlem’s southern fringe and the radius reflects that. Years are a best estimate.
source_quote: The joke, of course, is that I don't live in Harlem but in a border area.
source2_quote: I live rent-free in a building rented strictly to whites, in a section of the basement that was shut off and forgotten

household: with his daughter, the Little Girl (and Mameh until he drives her out)
creator: E. L. Doctorow
address_as_given: the flat on Hester Street
notes: The novel names Hester Street but no number or cross street; the point is mid-street and the radius covers the Lower East Side stretch of Hester. Source is the Internet Archive full-text search of scanned editions of the novel. Years are a best estimate.
source_quote: The flat on Hester Street had been abandoned. Evelyn took up the lease
source2_quote: Younger Brother around the Lower East Side in a futile search for Tateh and the little girl.

creator: E. L. Doctorow
address_as_given: Harlem
notes: The novel says only that he lives in Harlem. Source is the Internet Archive full-text search of scanned editions. Years are a best estimate.
source_quote: of the drive from Harlem, where Coalhouse Walker Jr. lived, and the drive back

creator: Bret McKenzie, Jemaine Clement and James Bobin
address_as_given: 227 Henry Street
notes: Pilot episode ("Sally") only, per the same fan site, which says the apartment "is now" at 28 Henry Street in the next episode.
source_quote: Bret and Jemaine are stalked by their only fan Mel (Kristen Schaal) outside their apartment at 227 Henry Street.

creator: J. J. Abrams and Matt Reeves
address_as_given: her dorm at the fictional University of New York, Greenwich Village
notes: Freshman-year dorm at the fictional UNY, modeled on NYU. The show was mostly filmed at USC in Los Angeles, so no New York exterior is recorded.
source_quote: Like NYU, UNY is located in Greenwich Village near Washington Square Park
source2_quote: The University of New York was supposed to be in Greenwich Village.

creator: J. J. Abrams and Matt Reeves
address_as_given: 170 Wooster Street
notes: The show gives this address. City tax-lot records list Wooster Street addresses only up to 160, at Houston Street, so 170 appears not to exist; the point is the north end of Wooster in SoHo. Years are a best estimate.
source_quote: The amazing loft apartment that Sean and Ben live in is given the address of 170 Wooster Street

creator: Dick Wolf
address_as_given: 203 West 89th Street
notes: The address appears on screen in her personal information in the season 6 episode "Pure" (2005). The source is Dick Wolf’s own production company. City tax-lot records show no lot addressed 203 West 89th, so the number may belong to a corner building or be made up; geocoded to the corner. She later moves (season 15) to an apartment with no address found.
source_quote: Benson’s Apartment Where: 203 West 89th Street, Upper West Side Though this isn’t where Benson’s apartment scenes have been filmed, this address was listed in her personal information

creator: Adrienne Kennedy
address_as_given: the top floor of a brownstone in the West Nineties
notes: Quoted from the play text via Internet Archive full-text search. The West Nineties span roughly ten blocks, so this is graded as neighborhood. Years are a best estimate.
source_quote: the top floor of a brownstone in the West Nineties in New York, a room filled with my
source2_quote: lives in a brownstone in the West 90s of Manhattan

work: Frankie and Johnny in the Clair de Lune
creator: Terrence McNally
address_as_given: a one-room walkup in Hell's Kitchen
notes: A reviewer reports that McNally's stage directions set the apartment in Hell's Kitchen; the publisher says Manhattan's West Side. I did not see the script itself. Other reviews say the West Fifties.
source_quote: McNally proscribes that we are in a one-room walkup in Hell’s Kitchen
source2_quote: In Frankie’s apartment on Manhattan’s West Side, she and her colleague Johnny are in bed together.

creator: Louise Fitzhugh
address_as_given: Eighty-second (Street), at the top of a dilapidated rooming house
notes: The book names the street but not the block; East 82nd is inferred from Harriet’s Yorkville route. A Criminal Element essay puts him on East 88th, which the text does not support.
source_quote: Harrison Withers lived on Eighty-second at the top of a dilapidated rooming house.

creator: Louise Fitzhugh
address_as_given: a private house around the corner
notes: The book places the house only "around the corner" on Harriet’s Yorkville route. Henderson Place is one essayist’s guess, not the author’s, so the point sits between it and Harriet’s block.
source_quote: She had discovered a way into a private house around the corner.
source2_quote: Mosey on up to Henderson Place, a little private street just off of East 86th and admire the houses and imagine Harriet sneaking into one to eavesdrop

creator: Terence Young
address_as_given: a basement apartment in Greenwich Village
notes: The film, like the play, gives no street address. Its exterior was shot on St. Luke's Place.
source_quote: 4 St. Luke's Place in Greenwich Village, Manhattan, was used as the exterior of Susy Hendrix's apartment building.

creator: Terence Young
address_as_given: 4 St. Luke's Place
notes: The house used for the outside of Susy Hendrix's building.
source_quote: 4 St. Luke's Place in Greenwich Village, Manhattan, was used as the exterior of Susy Hendrix's apartment building.
